title: Capcom's Notification of "CAPCOM ID Unauthorized Access" Received, but Isn't Their Security Configuration Way Too Lax?
content_md:
I recently received a data breach notification email from Capcom titled "Apology and Notice Regarding Customer Information Affected by Unauthorized Access to CAPCOM ID." The email alias service I use, SimpleLogin, flagged this official notice with the following warning right at the top: "This email failed anti-phishing checks when it was received by SimpleLogin, be careful with its content." Upon checking the actual email headers, it was configured as follows: ARC-Authentication-Results: i=1; mail.protonmail.ch; dmarc=fail (p=none dis=none) header.from=capcom.com; spf=pass smtp.mailfrom=fc8573.cn-0005.jp; dkim=pass (1024-bit key) header.d=dkim.cuenote.jp header.i=[@]dkim.cuenote.jp It is a DMARC authentication failure (dmarc=fail) .
